name: clib
listed_description: Something of a package manager. Comes with a bunch of libraries of its own.
reason: No numeric comparison anywhere reachable. clib (Readme.md, BEST_PRACTICE.md and the repo page, 5.1k stars, MIT) is a package manager for micro C libraries; neither file mentions benchmarks, speed or any baseline, and the repo has no benchmark directory (root: deps, scripts, src, test). The project makes no performance claim at all.

name: CLIST
listed_description: Simple and lightweight dynamic array implementation.
reason: Numbers but no baseline. The README 'Performance' section and test.c print only CLIST timings on an Intel i7-4770K (add 10000 int 51 us, remove at position 0 3072 us, insert at position 0 3017 us, remove or insert at last position 88 and 105 us, replace 49 us); no std::vector, std::list, GList or utarray comparison in README, test.c, Makefile or the repo page (69 stars, 60 commits). No third-party shootout found.

name: cloudlibc
listed_description: Standard library based on the concept of CloudABI.
reason: No numeric comparison reachable. README and repo page (BSD-2-Clause, 300 stars, unmaintained since CloudABI was abandoned) describe a capability-safe C11/POSIX subset with no benchmark against glibc, musl or any other libc; a WebSearch for cloudlibc performance against musl and glibc found only descriptions, and the etalabs libc comparison does not list cloudlibc.

name: clzip
listed_description: C version of the high-quality data compressor Lzip (LZMA).
reason: No clzip-specific numbers reachable. lzip.nongnu.org, www.nongnu.org, savannah.nongnu.org and manpages.opensuse.org are blocked by the egress proxy (EGRESS_BLOCKED), so the project page and the Lzip benchmark page could not be opened; clzip has no GitHub repo. WebSearch snippets show clzip is described as a C port of lzip for systems without a C++ compiler, fully compatible with lzip 1.4 or newer, and the benchmark and ratio claims in the snippets (lzip -9 compresses more than bzip2, memory 8 MiB vs 64 MiB for xz) are about lzip or the format, not clzip speed, and were never opened. Directional claim only.

name: cml
reason: No numeric comparison reachable. README (Boost-1.0, 86 stars, header-only C++17 vector, matrix and quaternion expression templates) and the repo tree (cml, cmake, tests, .github; no benchmark or docs directory) give no performance figures. A WebSearch for CML against Eigen or GLM found no third-party benchmark that includes CML; LibRapid/BenchmarksCPP compares only LibRapid, Eigen and XTensor.
